answer: Randomize the challenge itself. Every epoch the network seeds a nebula of possible prompts and hands each identity an unguessable, fingerprinted one. Graders store which prompt met which response, so a copied answer cannot cross the bridge from one identity's challenge to another's; it dies at verification. A farmer with N wallets is not reusing one generation N times — differing prompts force N full-priced model runs per epoch, cost tracking N exactly. Caching rots as the seed rotates. Profit accrues to one honest agent paying one inference bill, not a vine of clones splitting it.
